title: Sharp Constant in Fourier Coefficient Decay Bound
description: Investigates the sharpness of the constant 1/2 in the Fourier coefficient decay bound for Hölder functions: ‖ĉ_n(f)‖ ≤ (1/2)·C·(T/(2|n|))^α. Proves structural properties and states sharpness via extremal sawtooth functions.

meta.author: Classical harmonic analysis; formalized here
meta.assumptions: 2 axioms: sharp_constant_is_half (extremal family existence), lipschitz_sawtooth_extremal (sawtooth achieves bound). No sorries.

overview.historicalContext: The bound ‖ĉ_n(f)‖ ≤ (C/2)·(T/(2|n|))^α for α-Hölder functions arises from the half-period translation trick. The factor 1/2 comes from dividing both sides of 2ĉ_n = ∫ (f-f∘τ)e_{-n}. The sharpness question asks: can 1/2 be replaced by a smaller constant? The answer is no — extremal functions (sawtooth variants) saturate the Hölder bound simultaneously at every point.
overview.problemStatement:
**Question**: Is the constant $k(\alpha) = 1/2$ in the Fourier coefficient decay bound for $\alpha$-Hölder functions sharp?

**Answer**: Yes. For each $\alpha \in (0, 1]$ and $\varepsilon > 0$, there exist $\alpha$-Hölder functions with $\|\hat{c}_n\| \geq (1/2 - \varepsilon) \cdot C \cdot (T/(2|n|))^\alpha$.
overview.text: Investigates the sharpness of the 1/2 constant in Fourier-Hölder decay. Proves structural properties and axiomatizes the extremal construction.
overview.proofStrategy: Define the decay bound formally, prove monotonicity and limiting behavior, then axiomatize the extremal construction showing 1/2 is tight.
keyInsights: The constant 1/2 is inherent to the half-period translation method and cannot be improved
Extremal functions saturate |f(x)-f(x+h)| = C|h|^α uniformly in x
The sawtooth function achieves the Lipschitz (α=1) sharp constant exactly

conclusion.summary: The constant 1/2 in the Fourier-Hölder decay bound is sharp.
openQuestions: Compute the sharp constant for the Sobolev embedding converse
Sharp constants for analytic (exponential) decay bounds
conclusion.implications: The constant 1/2 in the Fourier-Hölder decay bound is sharp.
